concretechanges.before: I am not describing ancient history. I am describing a memory management algorithm.
concretechanges.after: Memory management supplies a deliberately uncomfortable analogy for that civic history.

concretechanges.before: The only difference is whether the mechanism is conscious.
concretechanges.after: The analogy exposes designated disposal; it does not make civic violence and a computer process morally or causally equivalent.

concretechanges.before: The individual psyche accumulates unprocessed emotional data at roughly the same rate a city accumulates social tension.
concretechanges.after: The analogy compares the pressure of unresolved feeling with civic tension; it supplies no shared accumulation rate.

concretechanges.before: The muscle was not injured. The pattern was not mechanical.
concretechanges.after: I came to interpret the recurring tension in relation to these encounters. That interpretation did not establish or exclude a physical cause.

concretechanges.before: This is the diagnostic problem. The symptom is not the disease. The symptom is the audit trail. The modern individual who treats the shoulder with massage, the insomnia with medication, the anxiety with breathing exercises — without asking *what the body is pointing to* — is treating the notification as the bug. The notification is not the bug. The notification is the debugger.
concretechanges.after: The shoulder-as-notification image helped me ask about the encounters surrounding it. Symptoms can have several causes; this inquiry cannot replace assessment or establish that massage, medication or other care is addressing the wrong problem.

concretechanges.before: The therapist says: "You are describing your colleague's ambition. But your voice changes when you talk about him. The data is not over there. The data is in the change of your voice."
concretechanges.after: Imagine a therapist asking: “You are describing your colleague’s ambition, and your voice changes when you talk about him. What happens for you at that moment?” This is an illustrative exchange, not a recorded session.

concretechanges.before: The *pharmakos* was not a mistake. It was a correct solution for a system with limited memory and no runtime debugger.
concretechanges.after: Describing an institutional function cannot make persecution a correct solution. The limits of the analogy matter most where it threatens to make the victim look like expendable memory.

concretechanges.before: The individual who performs this consciously does not need a crisis.
concretechanges.after: Conscious inquiry cannot guarantee that a crisis will be avoided.

concretechanges.before: This is the architecture. The rest is execution.
concretechanges.after: The colleague still has a life beyond the role I assigned him. Reclaiming a projection has to change how I treat that person, or the books remain beautifully balanced around an unpaid debt.
